intro.title: About Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal
intro.welcome: Welcome to **Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal**, widely recognized as the central **Quisqueya Stadium**. Located in the heart of **Santo Domingo**, **Distrito Nacional**, **Dominican Republic**, this destination serves as a primary hub for baseball fans and travelers visiting the region.
intro.description: In the Dominican Republic, baseball is not just a sport; it's a religion. Join tens of thousands of passionate fans, accompanied by Latin music, local Presidente beer, and cheerleader chants, to experience an adrenaline-pumping LIDOM game. This is the shared home of two legendary Dominican baseball teams: Tigres del Licey and Leones del Escogido.

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: ⚾ Dual Home (Winter Exclusive): During the LIDOM season from October to January, come witness the century-old rivalry between Licey (Tigers) and Escogido (Lions). (Note: Off-season visits offer exterior sightseeing and historical tours of the surrounding area)
🍻 Authentic Food: Enjoy classic Dominican snacks and ice-cold beer in the stands.
🌟 Hall of Fame Tribute: Pay respects to the statue and honors of the great pitcher Juan Marichal.
🏟️ Top Atmosphere: Feel the passionate cheers of approximately 14,465 spectators.

nearby.title: Landmarks & Attractions Around Quisqueya Stadium in Santo Domingo
nearby.lead: When visiting **Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal**, travelers can easily explore surrounding historical landmarks and points of interest, including **Zona Colonial (Colonial City)** and **Parque Mirador del Sur**, plus the Malecón waterfront and Faro a Colón.

items.name: Zona Colonial (Colonial City)
items.note: The oldest colonial city in the Americas, about 15 minutes by car from the stadium, full of 16th-century monuments, plazas and museums.

items.name: Parque Mirador del Sur
items.note: A large urban park with gardens, trails and viewpoints along the southern edge of the city, ideal for a relaxing stroll before a game.

items.name: Malecón de Santo Domingo
items.note: The famous seaside boulevard of the Dominican capital, lined with monuments, restaurants and ocean views.

items.name: Faro a Colón
items.note: The Columbus Lighthouse monument complex, one of the most recognizable landmarks of Santo Domingo.

items.q: Where is Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal located?
items.a: Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal is located in Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, Dominican Republic, at Avenida Tiradentes 3456 (Plus Code F3QF+7C Santo Domingo).

items.q: What is Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal commonly known as?
items.a: The stadium, widely recognized as Quisqueya Stadium, is the shared home of the Tigres del Licey and Leones del Escogido baseball clubs and hosts Dominican Professional Baseball League (LIDOM) games.

items.q: How many spectators can the stadium hold?
items.a: Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal has an approximate capacity of 14,465 spectators and is famous for its passionate atmosphere during the LIDOM season.

items.q: How can I get tickets to a baseball game?
items.a: Tickets depend on the game and event. It is recommended to buy them through the official Dominican Professional Baseball League (LIDOM) channels and book early for popular games.

items.q: Is the stadium open to visitors every day?
items.a: The stadium opens according to the schedule of games and events, mainly during the LIDOM season from October to January. Outside the season, visitors can enjoy exterior sightseeing. Always check the latest schedule before visiting.

items.q: What can I visit around Quisqueya Stadium in Santo Domingo?
items.a: Around the stadium you can easily explore Santo Domingo landmarks such as Zona Colonial (Colonial City), Parque Mirador del Sur, the Malecón waterfront and Faro a Colón.

items.q: Does Quisqueya Stadium host concerts or events besides baseball?
items.a: Baseball is its main use, but special events and concerts are announced through official channels such as LIDOM, the teams and local press. To find out what is on at the stadium today or in the coming days, always check the latest official announcements before planning your visit.

amenities.subtitle: Practical guidance on restrooms, parking, dining, accommodation, shopping, fuel and more near the stadium.
amenities.disclaimer: Neutrality note: This is an independent, non-profit educational website. We do not recommend any specific business. The list below only describes the general types of facilities available, so you can choose freely according to your own needs.

categories.title: Restrooms & Accessibility
items: Public restrooms are available near the main gates and on the concourses on game and event days.
Accessible restrooms and reserved seating exist at the stadium; on-site staff can assist visitors with reduced mobility.
On non-event days, restrooms in nearby shopping centres, parks and restaurants are a convenient option.

categories.title: Parking
items: Street parking and paid surface lots around the venue fill up quickly on game days, so plan to arrive early.
Official parking areas and valet service operate for major events; follow local signage and on-site staff directions.
If you prefer not to drive, taxi and ride-hailing drop-off zones near the gates are an easy alternative.

categories.title: Dining & Snacks
items: Concession stands inside the stadium serve typical ballpark snacks, hot food and drinks on event days.
The surrounding neighbourhood offers a wide range of restaurants, from casual dining to quick-service options, covering Dominican dishes and international cuisines.
Lines grow before game time, so arriving a little early makes it easier to enjoy your meal at a relaxed pace.

categories.title: Where to Stay
items: Most visitors stay in central districts such as Gazcue, Naco, Piantini or Ensanche La Fe, all within a short drive of the stadium.
Hotels, hostels and short-stay apartments across different price ranges are available in these neighbourhoods.
During the LIDOM season (October to January) and major events, it is wise to book accommodation well in advance.

categories.title: Shopping & Everyday Needs
items: Supermarkets and convenience stores operate in the surrounding neighbourhoods for everyday shopping.
ATMs are available near the stadium; carrying some cash is recommended for street food and small vendors.
Pharmacies can be found nearby, and hospitals and clinics are a short drive away if needed.

categories.title: Fuel, EV & Getting Around
items: Gas stations operate along Avenida Tiradentes and other main roads, convenient for refuelling rental cars.
Public electric-vehicle charging points are still limited in the city, so plan charging carefully if you rent an EV.
Consider a full tank before heading to the airport or to the countryside after the game.

story.title: Story & Culture: From Quisqueya to Juan Marichal
story.subtitle: How a 1955 ballpark became one of the living cathedrals of Dominican baseball
story.note: Educational note: this page is an independent, non-profit resource. Historical details follow public records and official sources, and may evolve over time.

parts.heading: A Name That Means 'Mother of All Lands'
parts.text: Quisqueya is the poetic name the Taíno people gave to the island of Hispaniola and, later, to the Dominican Republic. Choosing it for the capital's new ballpark in the 1950s was a statement of national pride: **Estadio Quisqueya** would be not just a stadium, but a stage for the country's favourite game.

parts.heading: The Night Baseball Came Alive (1955)
parts.text: The venue opened on **October 23, 1955** and made history under the floodlights in its very first game: a night match between **Tigres del Licey** and **Estrellas Orientales**. It was the first ballpark in the Dominican Republic equipped with lighting, carrying professional baseball into the evening and opening a new era for fans who worked during the day.

parts.heading: Two Giants Sharing One Home
parts.text: Few ballparks anywhere can claim what this one does: it is simultaneously the home of **two** professional winter-league clubs - the **Tigres del Licey** (founded in 1907) and the **Leones del Escogido** (founded in 1921). Their rivalry, the 'Clásico' of Dominican baseball, makes a night at Quisqueya feel like a living museum of passion and tradition.

parts.heading: A Name That Honours a Legend: Juan Marichal
parts.text: In **2015**, Law 11-15 officially renamed the venue **Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal**, in honour of the pitcher from Monte Cristi who dazzled Major League Baseball in the 1960s as the 'Dominican Dandy' and became the first Dominican player inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame (1983). The silhouette and logo that greet visitors today are a daily tribute to his legacy.

parts.heading: Stage of the Caribbean Series and International Nights
parts.text: Because of its atmosphere and tradition, Quisqueya has hosted the **Caribbean Series** ten times - most recently in **2022** - when the champions of the Caribbean leagues meet. In **2024**, the stadium welcomed a historic MLB World Tour game between the Boston Red Sox and the Tampa Bay Rays, and further international events are planned in the coming years.

parts.heading: The Sound of Dominican Baseball
parts.text: A game at Quisqueya is as much a musical experience as a sporting one: merengue and bachata over the public-address system, trumpets, drums and whistles in the stands, fans chanting for Licey or Escogido, and vendors walking the aisles with empanadas, yaniqueques and cold Presidente beer. For many Dominicans, this is where the heartbeat of the country can be felt every winter.

officialManagement.title: About Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal
officialManagement.text: Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal is a famous baseball stadium in Santo Domingo, featuring rich baseball history and excellent sports facilities. It is an important sports and cultural landmark loved by local residents and tourists.

historyTimeline.title: History & Significance of Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal

items.title: Official Opening
items.description: The stadium was officially inaugurated, built under the direction of dictator Trujillo (originally named Estadio Trujillo).

items.title: First LIDOM Match
items.description: Hosted the first Dominican Professional Baseball League (LIDOM) match, opening a new era for Dominican baseball.

items.title: Tribute to Juan Marichal
items.description: To honor the great pitcher Juan Marichal, the first Dominican inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame, the stadium was officially renamed Estadio Quisqueya Juan Marichal.

items.title: Caribbean Series
items.description: Has hosted the Caribbean Series (Serie del Caribe) multiple times, becoming one of the highest temples of Latin American baseball.

historyTimeline.guideContent: When visiting, you can start by entering the stadium area from the main entrance on Avenida Tiradentes; then walk around the stadium to enjoy the architecture and exterior landscapes; if you have enough time, you can learn about the stadium's baseball history and cultural value. Finally, explore the urban scenery around the stadium and feel the charm of the Dominican capital.
